mainEntity.name: How much does a Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fully rebuilt B4204T48 petrol engine for a Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine typically costs £5,500-£8,500 supply-only or £6,500-£10,000 fitted. Used units start from £2,800, and reconditioned options sit between £4,500-£6,500. ERAD replacement is a separate cost - £3,500-£5,500 for the electric rear motor. Hybrid system integration requires Volvo-specialist fitting (adds £650-£1,300). All EnginesMarket quotes include 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the first signs of ERAD failure in a Volvo XC60 T8?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning signs of ERAD failure include: a grinding or whining noise from the rear axle, a sudden loss of electric drive/power to the rear wheels, a "Hybrid System Failure" warning on the dashboard, and reduced acceleration from standstill. Warning lights may appear with no immediate driving change - get a diagnostic immediately. Early detection can sometimes allow bearing rebuild instead of full ERAD replacement. Ignoring early symptoms can lead to complete electric rear axle failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2017-2018 XC60 T8 worth £8,000-£12,000, a £6,000 engine replacement may be borderline unless the vehicle is in otherwise excellent condition with low mileage. For vehicles worth over £12,000, replacement is typically viable. The larger 2020+ T8 battery upgrade increases value - replacement more likely worth it. Compare the cost of a rebuilt unit with warranty vs. scrapping and replacing the whole car. We always recommend a specialist inspection before any decision.

mainEntity.name: How reliable is the Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine petrol engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.0-litre VEA petrol engine in the T8 is generally robust but has known issues: timing chain tensioner wear on pre-2020 examples and supercharger clutch failure. With proper maintenance (annual oil changes, 80k-mile timing chain inspection), many T8s exceed 150,000 miles without major petrol engine failure. The ERAD unit is the bigger reliability concern than the petrol engine. 2020-onward B4204T48 units have improved timing chain durability. Regular oil changes using Volvo-spec oil are critical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full petrol engine replacement on a Volvo XC60 T8 typically takes 4-6 working days for a specialist (8-10 days for a main dealer) due to the complex hybrid system integration. ERAD-only replacement is faster - 2-3 days. Supply & fit providers offer courtesy vehicle options. We recommend booking with a Volvo-hybrid trained specialist.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the XC60 T8 and the XC60 B5 or B6?

acceptedAnswer.text: The T8 Twin Engine is a plug-in hybrid with up to 455hp, a petrol engine driving the front wheels and an electric motor driving the rear axle with 18.8kWh battery. The B5 and B6 are mild hybrids with a 48V system - they have no plug-in capability, smaller battery packs, no ERAD unit, and significantly lower power output (250hp-300hp). The T8's ERAD is unique to the plug-in hybrid models. The petrol engine in the T8 is the B4204Txx family; B5/B6 use B420T and B420T2 variants. If you're replacing the engine on a T8, the ERAD must be checked separately.

historyTimeline.h2: Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Launched in 2017 as the flagship plug-in hybrid variant of the second-generation XC60, the T8 Twin Engine combined a turbocharged and supercharged 2.0-litre petrol engine with an electric motor driving the rear axle. The powertrain has evolved through battery capacity increases and software updates, with the later Recharge badging distinguishing the improved electric range models from 2020 onward.

milestones.description: B4204T34, 2.0-litre turbocharged/supercharged petrol with 87hp electric motor, 407hp combined
B4204T39 introduced, 2.0-litre T8 with 320hp petrol plus 87hp electric motor, 407hp combined
B4204T48, 2.0-litre T8 Recharge with 318hp petrol plus 145hp electric motor, 462hp combined; larger 11.6kWh battery
B4204T56, 2.0-litre T8 Recharge with 310hp petrol plus 145hp electric motor, 455hp combined; 18.8kWh battery
B4204Txx (current generation T8) with 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol, 314hp plus 145hp electric motor, 459hp combined

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - including the critical ERAD (Electric Rear Axle Drive) unit that distinguishes this plug-in hybrid from conventional XC60 models.

commonProblems.h2: Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The T8 Twin Engine powertrain is a complex, high-performance plug-in hybrid with two distinct failure points: the 2.0-litre petrol engine (B4204Txx family) and the ERAD (Electric Rear Axle Drive) unit. While the petrol engine itself is generally robust, the ERAD is the most common high-cost failure on higher-mileage T8s, and the 2.0-litre engine can suffer known VEA-family issues as it ages. Rebuilt T8 engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: ERAD (Electric Rear Axle Drive) Failure - Why the Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine Loses Rear Drive
problems.affectedModels: Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine (all B4204Txx codes, 2017-present)
problems.rootCause: Bearing wear or electrical failure within the rear electric motor unit. The ERAD is a sealed unit; failure typically results in complete loss of rear drive and hybrid system warning lights. Some early ERAD units (2017-2019) had higher-than-expected failure rates before Volvo revised the bearing design. [THIRD-PARTY]

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: ERAD unit removed, bearings replaced, refurbished electrical components
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early - but supply of rebuild kits is limited

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete new ERAD unit with warranty
Complete rebuilt petrol engine plus new ERAD, upgraded components on both

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2017-2020 Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine is worth £8,000-£25,000 depending on year, mileage, and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. ERAD replacement at £3,500-£5,500 is typically viable for any T8 worth over £10,000. A full petrol engine replacement (£5,500-£9,500) makes sense for vehicles worth £12,000+ where the owner intends to keep the car for 2+ years. For T8 examples below £8,000, evaluate both repair viability and the cost of a complete powertrain failure before committing.
problems.recommendation: ERAD failure is the single most expensive non-crash repair on a T8. If you have warning lights but the car still drives, get a diagnostic from a Volvo specialist immediately - caught early, ERAD rebuilds are significantly cheaper than full replacement. If the ERAD has already failed completely, a specialist replacement with warranty is almost always better value than a dealer new unit. For petrol engine failure, the rebuilt route with upgraded timing components typically offers better long-term value than used alternatives, especially on pre-2020 units.

problems.h4: Petrol Engine Timing Chain & Tensioner Wear - 2.0-Litre VEA Engine Issues
problems.affectedModels: Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine (B4204T34, B4204T39, 2017-2020)
problems.rootCause: The VEA-family 2.0-litre engine uses a timing chain system that can stretch or the tensioner can fail, particularly on early examples (2017-2019) with extended oil change intervals. Symptoms include a rattle on cold start and reduced performance. [THIRD-PARTY] [EM-INTERVIEW]

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chain, guides, tensioner, and sprocket replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Viable on any T8; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt petrol engine with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has already snapped, full replacement is the only safe option

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Timing chain replacement (£1,200-£1,800) is well within value for any T8 worth £8,000+. For 2017 examples with values at the lower end (£8k-£10k), the repair is still typically viable if the rest of the vehicle is in good condition.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a cold-start rattle from the B4204Txx engine, get the timing chain inspected immediately. A £1,200 specialist repair is far cheaper than a £5,500+ engine replacement. For 2017-2019 examples with no documented chain history, consider preventative replacement at 80,000 miles.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B4204T39 Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine engine prices

problems.h4: Supercharger Clutch Failure - Reduced Low-End Power on T8 Units
problems.affectedModels: Volvo XC60 T8 Twin Engine (B4204T34, B4204T39, 2017-2020)
problems.rootCause: The supercharger clutch can wear, causing intermittent or complete loss of supercharger engagement. Symptoms include a rattling noise at low RPM and a noticeable reduction in low-end torque (below 3,000rpm). [THIRD-PARTY]

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if clutch is the only issue
Recommended if there is any evidence of internal wear

problems.vehicleValueCheck: The £800-£1,200 clutch repair is viable on any T8 worth £6,000+. For higher-mileage examples, the complete supercharger replacement may be the more durable choice.
problems.recommendation: The supercharger clutch is a known weak point but is not catastrophic - it reduces performance but won't stop the car. However, if left unrepaired, the supercharger can fail completely, requiring a more expensive full unit replacement. For pre-2020 T8s, budget for this repair between 60k-100k miles.
